article.title: NFL EDGE Thursday Morning Brief
article.dek: The Rams ran Green Bay out of the game 26-13, Parsons got his sack in his debut — and the Week 12 board is finally live, with three cards on Sunday games.

items.headline: Rams 26, Packers 13 — Parsons got his sack, Green Bay got run over
paragraphs: The Rams beat the Packers 26-13 on Wednesday night in the first Thanksgiving Eve game. Green Bay tied it at 13 by halftime, then did not score again.

Micah Parsons made his season debut after 11 months out with a torn ACL. He played 27 snaps on a snap count and still got a sack of Matthew Stafford in the first half, with four pressures. The Rams just did not throw enough for him to take the game over — they ran it 47 times for 241 yards, with Blake Corum going for over 150.

Green Bay falls to 6-5 with a second straight loss. The Rams are 7-4. Packers receiver Christian Watson left the game late in the first half after a hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens, who was ejected, and did not return. No update on Watson yet.
items.takeaway: Parsons is back and looked explosive in a limited role, but the Rams ran Green Bay out of the game and the Packers' playoff path just got harder.

items.headline: Thursday injury board: Walker and Ferguson are out
paragraphs: Kenneth Walker III is out for Kansas City tonight in Buffalo with a groin injury. It is his third straight missed game. Rookie Emmett Johnson starts again.
Jake Ferguson is out for Dallas against Philadelphia. Dak Prescott is healthy. Joe Milton starts again at quarterback for the Eagles.

The final word on who plays comes with the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before each kickoff. Chicago at Detroit kicks off at 12:30 p.m. ET, Philadelphia at Dallas at 4:30 p.m. ET, Kansas City at Buffalo at 8:20 p.m. ET.
items.takeaway: Walker is out and Johnson starts again for Kansas City; Ferguson is out for Dallas and Milton starts again for Philadelphia. Inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff.

items.headline: Rain and wind tonight in Buffalo; Detroit and Dallas are indoors
paragraphs: Kansas City at Buffalo kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET in open air at Highmark Stadium. Rain is expected through the afternoon and night, with a 100% chance at kickoff, around 35 to 36 degrees, and wind out of the east-northeast around 18 to 19 mph, gusting near 30. A gale warning runs from 2:00 p.m. Thursday to 1:00 a.m. Friday.
Chicago at Detroit and Philadelphia at Dallas are both indoors, so weather is not a factor there.
items.takeaway: Tonight in Buffalo: rain all night, mid-30s, wind around 19 mph with gusts near 30. Detroit and Dallas play indoors.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The Week 12 board is live — and it has three cards
paragraphs: The board flipped overnight. Week 12 is up, all 16 games, and there are three headline cards, all on Sunday games.

Hit Rate is Cleveland on the moneyline at -230 on FanDuel. That is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. The model gives Cleveland about a 64.5% chance against Las Vegas, and it holds up to -238. Hit Rate is about win probability, not value — the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced is New England on the moneyline at -116 on FanDuel. That is the middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much, and a good starting point if you are newer to this. The model gives New England about a 58.3% chance against the Chargers, and it holds up to -119.

Value is the Chargers +1.5 at -115 on FanDuel. That is the model's plus-expected-value play, the one where the price looks better than the chance of it hitting. The model gives the Chargers about a 50.6% chance to cover, against a market price that implies about 46.2%, and it holds up to -118.

Yes, Balanced and Value are on opposite sides of the same game. That is fine. They answer different questions: Balanced asks what is a strong pick at a fair price, Value asks where the price is wrong. Read the card that matches the question you are asking.
items.takeaway: Three cards, all Sunday: Hit Rate is Cleveland moneyline -230, Balanced is New England moneyline -116, and Value is the Chargers +1.5 at -115 — the model's plus-expected-value play.

items.headline: The model is cooler than the market on all three Thanksgiving favorites
paragraphs: The model has Detroit beating Chicago by about 3.7 points. The market has Chicago as a 1.5-point favorite. That is a real gap, and it runs the other way from the board.

Same story in the other two games. The model has Dallas by about 4.8 over Philadelphia, while the market has Dallas -8.5. It has Buffalo by about 0.7 over Kansas City, while the market has Buffalo -3.

There is no card on any Thursday game. The board is not telling you to bet the other side. It is telling you the favorites are priced richer than the model likes. If your book has a Thursday number you like, type it into Check and let the app run it back through the model and evaluator. That is the verdict for your price.
items.takeaway: The model likes Detroit, Dallas and Buffalo by less than the market does, and it has no card on any Thursday game — use Check on your book's number.

items.headline: Closing line value: did you beat the close?
paragraphs: Closing line value is simple. It asks whether the price you took was better than the price the game closed at. If you bet a team at -2.5 and the line closes at -3.5, you got closing line value. You bought the same bet cheaper than the market ended up pricing it.

Hypothetical example: imagine you take the underdog at +3.5 on Monday. By Sunday the line has moved to +2.5. You hold a better number than anyone betting on Sunday can get. That does not mean your bet wins — the game still has to be played — but over a lot of bets, consistently beating the close is a sign you are finding good prices.

The flip side matters too. If you keep taking numbers that get worse by kickoff, you are paying more than the market thinks the bet is worth. That is a habit worth noticing, not a single result worth chasing.
items.takeaway: Beating the closing line does not guarantee a win, but consistently getting a better price than the close is one of the clearest signs you are betting well.

items.headline: Rams-Packers closed at -2.5, and the under cashed
paragraphs: The Rams opened -3.5 and closed -2.5, a move toward Green Bay that lined up with Parsons' return being priced in. The total slid from 46.5 to 44.5.
The final was 26-13, 39 points total. The under cashed, and the Rams covered the closing number — they won by 13 with the spread at 2.5. The move toward Green Bay did not pay off.
items.takeaway: Rams-Packers closed at -2.5 after opening -3.5, the total slid 46.5 to 44.5, and the Rams covered the closing number while the under cashed.

items.headline: A week of movement, now that the board has flipped
paragraphs: The board spent the week on Week 11, so this is the first morning it shows Week 12. That gives us a full week of movement to look back on, from where the lines opened last Sunday to where DraftKings has them this morning.

The biggest move was the Chargers flipping from favorite to underdog. They opened -3.5 against New England and are now +1.5. That is the same game the Value card is on, and it is why the price looks the way it does.

The Buffalo total fell from 51.5 to 45.5 as the rain forecast firmed up. The Giants went from -4 to -6 against Indianapolis, and Denver went from -2.5 to -4.5 against Pittsburgh. Dallas moved from -8 to -8.5, Chicago from -2.5 to -1.5.
These are the numbers on the board now, and the app has caught up with them. If your book is sitting off the board's number, run it through Check and get a verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: The Chargers flipped from -3.5 favorite to +1.5 underdog, the Buffalo total fell six points on the rain, and the Giants and Broncos both moved out. The board has caught all of it.

items.headline: Thanksgiving is a Check day — and log it honestly
paragraphs: Three games today, and the inactives for each one land about 90 minutes before kickoff. That is the one thing worth waiting on. If your book has a number you like, do not wait for a better one that may never come — type it into Check and let the app run it back through the model and evaluator.
The board refreshes every morning and evening, and the evening brief will have the Sunday board in full. For now, the three Sunday cards are the board's answers.
One more thing: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log today's results either way — the losers too.
items.takeaway: Wait for inactives about 90 minutes before each kickoff, then run your book's number through Check. And log today's results honestly, losers included.
